title: QUIC RFC 9000 Zero-Length Connection-ID Mode Runtime Architecture
purpose: Describe the bounded runtime path that honors zero-length connection-ID selection by suppressing local connection-ID issuance and using an empty Destination Connection ID for packets sent toward peers that selected zero-length mode.
design_summary: The runtime treats a local transport-parameter Initial Source Connection ID value with length zero as the local zero-length connection-ID selection. Once that fact is present, explicit local connection-ID issue events and replacement issuance after first use of a routed local CID are rejected before route, token, or NEW_CONNECTION_ID effects can be produced. For the peer-selected side, the runtime treats a peer transport-parameter Initial Source Connection ID value with length zero as requiring an empty Destination Connection ID on outbound packets. Peer transport-parameter commit installs the empty handshake destination ID so shared 1-RTT packet protection uses the zero-length DCID, and CurrentPeerDestinationConnectionId also reports empty before peer-issued CID, preferred-address, or handshake fallback state can override it.
data_and_state_considerations: Zero-length mode is derived from committed transport-parameter state rather than from ad hoc packet parsing. Local issuance suppression reads the committed local Initial Source Connection ID. Outbound peer selection reads the committed peer Initial Source Connection ID and updates the handshake coordinator's destination ID during peer transport-parameter commit so existing application-data send paths remain the single packet construction seam.
edge_cases_and_constraints: A local endpoint that selected zero-length mode must not issue a new connection ID explicitly or through replacement replenishment.
A peer that selected zero-length mode keeps outbound packets on an empty Destination Connection ID even if handshake fallback or preferred-address connection IDs exist.
Non-zero local and peer Initial Source Connection IDs keep existing connection-ID issuance and outbound DCID behavior.
The slice does not introduce a public API for selecting zero-length mode; it honors the transport-parameter state already published by the handshake path.
The slice does not claim multipath support or migration success for zero-length connection-ID deployments.
alternatives_considered: Only check CurrentPeerDestinationConnectionId; rejected because the shared application-data packet builder uses the handshake coordinator's stored destination ID.
Treat an unset local source connection ID as local zero-length mode; rejected because older tests and bootstrap paths can leave that value unset without intentionally selecting zero-length mode.
Add a broad host-facing zero-length mode API in this slice; rejected because the bounded requirement proof can derive the mode from committed transport parameters.
risks: Tests that directly mutate TLS bridge state can bypass runtime commit hooks; requirement-home proof commits peer parameters through runtime transition events.
The local-mode guard depends on local transport parameters being published before issuance attempts.
Zero-length mode deliberately limits connection-ID rotation and should not be combined with migration claims outside this artifact's scope.

supplemental_sections.heading: Scope
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers local no-issuance behavior after local zero-length CID selection and outbound 1-RTT Destination Connection ID selection toward peers that selected zero-length mode. It does not cover public configuration APIs, multipath, broad migration support, or HTTP/3 behavior.
